_about: Monday: myth vs fact carousels (5 slides: myth, fact, second fact or what it means, takeaway). Each item names the findings it uses as '<source id>/<finding id>' from sources.json; use their wording. status: ready, hold (needs Grade or a check first) or used. The Saturday run picks the first ready item that isn't used yet, skipping any that repeat a pillar used in the last 2 weeks.

items.myth: Sex toys are for people who can't find a partner.
If he finishes, the night went well for both of you.
items.takeaway: Her pleasure isn't a bonus round. Ask, and take your time.

items.myth: If it doesn't happen during intercourse, something is wrong with her.
items.takeaway: Most women need more than one kind of touch. That's normal, not a problem to fix.

items.myth: Vaseline or baby oil works fine as lube with a condom.
items.takeaway: With condoms, stick to water-based (or silicone-based) lube.

items.myth: One night it doesn't work means something is wrong with you.
items.takeaway: Now and then is normal. Often is a reason to see a doctor, not to feel ashamed.

items.myth: A little pain during sex is normal. You just bear it.
items.takeaway: Pain is a signal, not a duty. Stop, and get it checked.

items.myth: Past 60, intimacy is over.
items.takeaway: Desire doesn't retire. Health matters more than age.

items.myth: Needing lubricant means something is wrong with you.
items.takeaway: Lube is about comfort and pleasure, not a fix for a problem.
items.notes: No percentage from this paper (see source caution). Pair with a care tip: water-based lube is safe with silicone toys and condoms.

items.myth: Most men finish too fast.
items.takeaway: What you see online isn't the average. Pressure makes it worse; information makes it better.

items.myth: You either last long or you don't. It can't be learned.
items.takeaway: It's a skill, and skills can be practised.

items.myth: If you're not in the mood first, you don't really want them.
items.takeaway: Desire doesn't always knock. Sometimes it arrives once you begin.

items.myth: Sleep has nothing to do with desire.
items.takeaway: Sometimes the most romantic thing is an early night.

items.myth: Pleasure is a luxury, not self-care.
items.takeaway: Feeling good is part of looking after yourself, alongside sleep, food and people you trust.

items.myth: How often a man ejaculates has nothing to do with his health.
items.takeaway: A link worth knowing. Prostate checks still matter: talk to a doctor.

items.myth: Low mood and a low sex drive are two separate problems.
items.takeaway: If your mood has been low for weeks, talk to a doctor or a mental health professional. It's a strength, not a weakness.
items.notes: Must end with the professional-help pointer. Never suggest pleasure treats depression.

items.myth: Using a vibrator will numb you or ruin sex with a partner.
items.takeaway: Start on the lowest setting, take breaks, and enjoy it.

items.myth: Erection problems only happen to older men.
items.takeaway: It's common, it's not a failure, and a doctor can help. It can also be an early sign of heart or blood-sugar problems, so get checked.

items.myth: Pelvic floor exercises are only for women after childbirth.
items.takeaway: Men have a pelvic floor too. Ask a doctor or physiotherapist how to do the exercises properly.
items.notes: Never say 'treats' or 'cures'. Keep the 'small trial' wording.

items.myth: Happy couples have sex every day.
items.takeaway: Closeness matters more than keeping score.

items.myth: Talking about sex kills the mood.
items.takeaway: One honest question can do more than any trick.

items.myth: All lubricants are basically the same.
items.takeaway: Read the label: water-based, and as few extras as possible.
items.notes: Don't claim Intimova's lubricant passes these tests unless its product page says so. It is out of stock as of 27 Oct 2026.

items.myth: If sex isn't working for you, you're the only one.
items.takeaway: Common doesn't mean you have to accept it. Talk to your partner, and to a doctor if it hurts.

items.myth: After 40, intimacy just isn't supposed to matter.
items.takeaway: Changes in your 40s are common, and you still deserve pleasure. A doctor can help with the physical side.

items.myth: Struggling with desire or pleasure means you're broken.
items.takeaway: You're not broken. You're human, and you deserve support.

items.myth: A toy is a toy. The material doesn't matter.
items.takeaway: Look for body-safe silicone, and skip anything sold as 'jelly'.

items.myth: Dryness during sex is rare.
items.takeaway: It's common, and there's no shame in a little help.
items.notes: Hold: check the PMC8261092 paper first (see source caution).

items.myth: Once it's over, it's over.
items.takeaway: Stay a while. The moments after count too.
items.notes: Reserved for Friday's tip on 'staying close after'. Use here only if that tip is retired.
